findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/dev-memory.md still presents .koala/dev-memory and .koala/story paths as the storage contract, but B-5cc7 implementation now makes .lattice/dev-memory the canonical read/write path and adds .koala only as a read-only legacy fallback. The docs oracle therefore no longer describes the implemented path semantics; update the decision doc to state .lattice canonical storage plus .koala legacy read fallback, or adjust implementation to match the documented .koala contract.
findings.resolvedReason: Resolved by commit a24a78aa updating docs/requirements/decisions/dev-memory.md to make .lattice the canonical dev-memory/story-candidate storage, restrict .koala to read-only legacy fallback, rename commands to lattice dev_memory_*, and retain non-authoritative gateEvidence:false / authority:non_authoritative semantics. Verified with rg checks for stale Koala/.koala command/path claims and git diff --check.

findings.desc: Global dev-memory writes can still target the legacy KOALA_GLOBAL_MEMORY_DIR path, violating the story contract that .lattice is canonical writable storage and .koala is read-only fallback. docs/requirements/decisions/dev-memory.md:30-31 says legacy .koala files are read-only fallback and writes must not append to .koala. But packages/main/src/core/dev-memory.ts:178-181 resolves the writable global path from LATTICE_GLOBAL_MEMORY_DIR || KOALA_GLOBAL_MEMORY_DIR, and packages/main/src/handlers/dev-memory.ts:79-87 plus 214-226 append global capture/promotion through resolveGlobalMemoryPath. In a migrated shell with only KOALA_GLOBAL_MEMORY_DIR set, dev_memory_capture --scope=global or dev_memory_finish --scope=global appends to the legacy location instead of canonical ~/.lattice storage.
findings.resolvedReason: Resolved by commit 8f59161: resolveGlobalMemoryPath now only honors LATTICE_GLOBAL_MEMORY_DIR for writable global storage and otherwise uses canonical ~/.lattice/dev-memory/experience.jsonl. KOALA_GLOBAL_MEMORY_DIR remains available only through resolveLegacyGlobalMemoryPath / resolveGlobalMemoryReadPaths as read fallback. Focused smoke now asserts KOALA_GLOBAL_MEMORY_DIR alone cannot redirect the writable global path and that read paths remain current-first plus legacy fallback. Verified with npm --prefix packages/main run build && node packages/main/dist/tasks/dev-memory-legacy-read-smoke.js.

findings.desc: concept-cleanup: dev-memory legacy read fallback incomplete: packages/main/src/core/lattice-parallel-wave.ts still builds experienceRefs with readEntries(resolveProjectMemoryPath(...)) and readEntries(resolveGlobalMemoryPath()), bypassing readProjectMemoryEntries/readGlobalMemoryEntries. That read-only consumer therefore ignores legacy .koala project/global fallback and KOALA_GLOBAL_MEMORY_DIR fallback promised by F-002/docs.
findings.resolvedReason: Resolved by commit bf001e43: lattice-parallel-wave experienceRefs now use readProjectMemoryEntries/readGlobalMemoryEntries so parallel dispatch/report include the same .lattice canonical plus .koala read-only legacy fallback as other dev-memory read consumers. Scope expansion was explicitly acknowledged in scope-contract.json because F-003 identified this file as a necessary dev-memory projection consumer. Verified by npm --prefix packages/main run build && node packages/main/dist/tasks/dev-memory-legacy-read-smoke.js.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/dev-memory.md documents the dev-memory user-facing commands as lattice dev_memory_* (lines 75-96), matching the F-001/F-002 review expectation. The implementation mostly registers dev_memory_* under the lattice CLI, but dev_memory_start still emits legacy koala dev_memory_finish reminders in packages/main/src/handlers/dev-memory.ts:310-313. That leaves the decision doc and implementation guidance inconsistent on the required command prefix.
findings.resolvedReason: Resolved by commit bf001e43: dev_memory_start user-facing reminders now use lattice dev_memory_finish, lattice dev_memory_finish --scope=global, and lattice dev_memory_finish --storyId=<id>, matching docs/requirements/decisions/dev-memory.md. Focused smoke asserts lattice reminder is present and koala dev_memory_finish is absent.

findings.desc: Quality consistency confirmation of existing F-004: docs/requirements/decisions/dev-memory.md documents the user-facing dev-memory commands as lattice dev_memory_* after the .lattice canonical path update, but packages/main/src/handlers/dev-memory.ts:310-313 still tells users to run koala dev_memory_finish. That leaves the changed handler guidance inconsistent with the canonical Lattice command prefix and the F-001/F-002 resolution docs.
findings.resolvedReason: Resolved with the same concrete fix as B-5cc7:F-004 in commit bf001e43: dev_memory_start no longer emits koala dev_memory_finish guidance and the smoke test verifies the lattice command prefix.

findings.desc: B-5cc7:F-003 runtime path is fixed, but the parallel-wave truth-source doc still describes the old .koala-only dev-memory boundary. packages/main/src/core/lattice-parallel-wave.ts:313-330 now builds experienceRefs from readProjectMemoryEntries/readGlobalMemoryEntries, and docs/requirements/decisions/dev-memory.md:25-31 says .lattice is canonical read/write with .koala read-only legacy fallback. However docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-parallel-wave.md:152-157 still says parallel dispatch/report reads project memory from <projectRoot>/.koala/dev-memory/experience.jsonl and global memory from ~/.koala/dev-memory/experience.jsonl. That contradicts the implemented contract and the canonical dev-memory decision, so future consumers of the parallel-wave requirement would reimplement F-003 incorrectly.
findings.resolvedReason: Resolved by commit ca87d7b: docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-parallel-wave.md now documents .lattice canonical dev-memory reads, .koala read-only legacy fallback, KOALA_GLOBAL_MEMORY_DIR legacy global fallback, and non-authoritative experienceRefs fields consistent with dev-memory.md and the lattice-parallel-wave implementation. Scope expansion was explicitly acknowledged for the decision doc.
